name: Push API (Web Push)
plain: Lets a server wake the site in the background and show a notification.
meaning: Reaches the person after they leave the site. Every message must show a visible notification (userVisibleOnly), but the site learns when a device is online and which browser vendor push service it uses.

web.api: registration.pushManager.subscribe({userVisibleOnly: true, applicationServerKey}); push event; subscription.endpoint, getKey('p256dh'|'auth')

access.prompt_ui: Same notification prompt. subscribe() requires notifications permission first (Firefox and Safari also need a gesture). Safari on iOS only works for Home Screen web apps.
access.persistence: Subscription persists until unsubscribe(), 404 or 410 from the endpoint, expiry, or clearing site data; permission revocation deletes it
access.revocation: Site settings, unsubscribe(), pushsubscriptionchange event, 410 Gone responses
access.iframe: Service worker scope only; iframes cannot subscribe
steps: pushManager.subscribe with the VAPID public key
Send endpoint, p256dh and auth to your server
Server POSTs an encrypted message (RFC 8291) with VAPID JWT (RFC 8292) to the vendor endpoint
Browser wakes the service worker and fires push; the worker must call showNotification

safari.note: macOS 13 Ventura Web Push, gesture required

data.metric: Encrypted push message delivered to a service worker
data.update: any time while the browser runs; delivered after restart within TTL

fields.name: TTL
fields.range: 0 to 2,419,200 (4 weeks FCM maximum); messages expire

fields.name: Topic
fields.range: up to 32 URL-safe base64 characters; replaces an undelivered message with the same topic

fields.name: status codes
fields.range: 201 created, 400 bad request, 404 or 410 gone, 413 payload too large, 429 slow down with Retry-After

limits.headline: Can send you notifications after you leave, once you allow them
limits.user_action: You tap Allow on the notification pop up, or add the site to your iPhone Home Screen
can: Wake the site in the background and show a notification
Send news, chat or order updates you asked for
Learn when your device is online and which vendor's push service it uses
cannot: Send anything before you tap Allow
Send a message without a visible notification
Work on iPhone unless the site is a Home Screen web app
Keep going once you block or unsubscribe
limits.differs: On iPhone, only Home Screen web apps can receive push. Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on computers ask with the same prompt.

story.what_it_is: A site's server can wake your browser in the background and show a message when something new happens.

marketing.name: Push API
marketing.pitch: Lets a web app receive messages pushed from a server, even when the app is not loaded or running.

marketing.name: Web Push for iOS
marketing.pitch: Web apps added to the Home Screen can now receive push messages on iPhone and iPad, like native apps.

story.for_you: You tap Allow on a prompt, then the site can send alerts any time, even if the tab is closed. Alerts look like those from apps. You can turn them off in browser settings.
story.for_makers: Makers get a direct line to the person with no app store, no email and no ad cost. It is used for messages, news, sales and live events. The browser's own push service delivers the message.

use_cases.example: A web chat sends a push for each new message, so you reply even when the tab is closed.
A browser strategy game pushes a note when an attack lands or your build ends.
A sports site pushes a goal alert in the last minute of a match.
A store pushes a flash sale or back in stock alert.
A news site pushes breaking stories to subscribers.
A ride web app pushes your driver's arrival.
A push ad network buys placement in alerts, and may send false alert scams.
A bank pushes a card spend alert to confirm a payment is yours.

technical_bounds: Chrome and Safari require userVisibleOnly: true; hidden pushes are not allowed
Firefox allows a limited number of silent pushes, quota resets when the site is visited
Subscription endpoint is a capability URL: anyone holding it can send messages (with VAPID key)
Browser closed on desktop means delivery waits until it reopens (within TTL)

abuse: Tracking when a device is online

history.change: Push API ships with GCM, later FCM
VAPID required for new FCM subscriptions in Chrome
Web Push on macOS via web.push.apple.com, standards based VAPID
